newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER - DUTCH POLICE INTERVIEW SOCCER STAR IN RAPE CHARGE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER - DUTCH POLICE INTERVIEW SOCCER STAR IN RAPE CHARGE.

text.p: Police said on Friday they had interviewed Dutch soccer international Patrick Kluivert in connection with a rape charge brought by an Amsterdam woman.
"Kluivert and a friend reported to the police voluntarily on Thursday and we took a statement," police spokesman Klaas Wilting said.
The unnamed friend had also been involved in the alleged incident along with the 20-year old former Ajax Amsterdam striker and two other men, Wilting said.
Wilting confirmed police had destroyed evidence related to the case after the woman initially decided against pressing charges, but he declined comment on how this would affect the investigation.
"The case will be submitted to the public prosecutor for his decision in due course," he said.
Dutch newspaper De Telegraaf, which published the original allegations, said Kluivert had flown in from South America especially to talk to police.
In May last year Kluivert was convicted of causing death by dangerous driving.
He was subsequently ordered to carry out 240 hours of community service and received a three month jail sentence, suspended for two years.
Kluivert signed a four-year deal with AC Milan in February this year and is due to start there next season, teaming up with former Ajax colleagues and close friends Edgar Davids and Michael Reiziger.
